item.title: Brad Lightcap, a Top OpenAI Executive, Steps Down
item.author: Emmy Martin
item.content:encoded: Brad Lightcap, a longtime leader, said he was starting a new venture. His exit from the artificial intelligence company is the latest in a series there.

item.title: Flock Cameras Can Track Every Car in America. Police Love Them. Citizens Don’t.
item.author: Fernando Alfonso III and Kashmir Hill
item.content:encoded: In Texas, there’s one thing liberals and conservatives agree on: They don’t want cameras trained on their cars.

item.title: Redpoint’s Brescia on Nvidia’s $500B Funding, AI Capex
item.content:encoded: Erica Brescia, Managing Director at Redpoint Ventures, discussed Super Micro's robust business model and strong market position during the segment. Despite recent volatility, Super Micro benefits from significant pricing power and a durable business model as a key supplier of hardware components essential for AI-driven growth. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Upwork CEO on AI Disruption Concerns, Earnings Slide
item.content:encoded: Hayden Brown, CEO of Upwork, discusses the company's recent financial performance after its full-year forecast missed analyst estimates, leading to a significant drop in the stock price. Brown discusses the sources of pressure facing Upwork and how the company plans to adapt to these challenges. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Accel Raises $3.5 Billion to Invest in Emerging Global AI Startups
item.author: Natasha Mascarenhas
item.content:encoded: Accel, a global venture capital firm with offices in Silicon Valley, London and Bangalore, India, has raised $3.5 billion in new funds for early-stage investments across the world.

item.title: Google to Add Three Subsea Cable Systems Across the Americas
item.author: Antonia Mufarech
item.content:encoded: Alphabet Inc.’s Google announced new cable links in the Americas on Tuesday, including one between Panama, the Dominican Republic and Chile, which is trying to establish itself as a regional digital hub.

item.title: CoreWeave Took a Step in the Right Direction, Gil Luria Says
item.content:encoded: Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, reacts to CoreWeave topping analysts' estimates for second-quarter sales after signing up more customers in a booming market, with sales more than doubling to $2.58 billion. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SiTime CEO on Role in AI Data Centers, Renesas Deal
item.content:encoded: Rajesh Vashist, Chairman and CEO of SiTime, discussed the company's impressive triple-digit year-over-year revenue growth, attributing much of the acceleration to AI-driven demand and the expanding data center market. SiTime's technology plays a critical role in timing synchronization across various data center components, including TPUs, GPUs, switches, accelerator cards, optical modules, and cables, ensuring high performance and cost efficiency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vertiv CEO on AI Infrastructure Buildout, Supply Chain
item.content:encoded: Gio Albertazzi, CEO of Vertiv, joined the program to discuss the company's recent earnings report. Unlike many AI-related companies that often beat revenue expectations but miss on profitability or margins, Vertiv reported the opposite: it beat on margins and profitability but missed on revenue. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3: A New Contender in the US-China AI Race: Podcast
item.author: K Oanh Ha and Yang Yang
item.content:encoded: Chinese startup Moonshot has put the AI world on notice. On today’s Big Take Asia podcast: What Kimi K3 means for the future of the global race for AI supremacy.

item.title: AI Infrastructure Boom Drives Market Movers | Closing Bell
item.content:encoded: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Isabelle Lee, Kristine Aquino and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Shares Surge After Booming AI Demand Bolsters Outlook
item.author: Dina Bass and Brody Ford
item.content:encoded: CoreWeave Inc., a provider of computing that powers artificial intelligence systems, soared in late trading after the AI spending frenzy spurred faster sales growth than anticipated.

item.title: Super Micro Gives Sales Outlook That Tops Rosiest Projection
item.author: Dina Bass
item.content:encoded: Super Micro Computer Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that topped analysts’ estimates, a sign the booming artificial intelligence market continues to bolster sales of the company’s servers.

item.title: Spotify Will Label A.I. Artists and Avoid Promoting Them
item.author: Malia Mendez
item.content:encoded: The new label, which will begin to be applied next month, is an effort by the streaming service to be more transparent about A.I.-generated music on its app.

item.title: Bitcoin Wallet Hack Shakes Industry | Bloomberg Crypto 8/11/2026
item.content:encoded: "Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: Galaxy Digital Head of Firmwide Research Alex Thorn, ledger Chief Human Agency officer Ian Rogers, Bitwise Asset Management CIO Matt Hougan, Robinhood Crypto General Manager Johann Kerbrat, and AnchorWatch COO & Co-Founder Becca Amilee Rubenfeld. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Athena Capital Sees Opportunities in AI Infrastructure
item.content:encoded: Isabelle Freidheim, Founder and Managing Partner at Athena Capital, discusses investment opportunities in the AI sector, emphasizing that much of the AI model layer has already been built, funded, and repriced outside public markets. She explains that current public market activity around AI models largely represents liquidity events rather than new capital raising. Freidheim highlights that the real growth potential lies in companies involved in deploying AI infrastructure, which will provide investors with earlier and cleaner exposure to AI's expansion phase, as infrastructure names come to market over the next few years. This approach contrasts with investing in areas that are already fully priced, such as the AI model layer itself. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin Will 'Survive' Cold Wallet Hack: Alex Thorn
item.content:encoded: Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The crypto community is reeling from a breach involving Coldcard wallets made by Coinkite, that drained an estimated $130 million of Bitcoin from about 7,300 wallet addresses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Brave New World' With AI Tied To Hacks: Ledger's Rogers
item.content:encoded:
Ian Rogers, chief human agency officer at Ledger, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The crypto community is reeling from a breach involving Coldcard wallets made by Coinkite. Rogers, who's company is a competitor of Coinkites, discusses how AI has made crypto hacks easier than ever.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Family Crypto Deal Ends In Investor Rout
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg's Nicola White joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." A virtually unknown fintech that catapulted into the headlines and cracked a $1 billion market value after signing a deal with the Trump family’s crypto platform last year has sold its core business for about $12 million. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: May Be At Bottom of Crypto Winter: Bitwise's Hougan
item.content:encoded: Matt Hougan, CIO of Bitwise Asset Management, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The Coldcard wallet hack may strengthen the case for spot Bitcoin ETFs by undermining confidence in self-custody among investors. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin Will 'Survive' Cold Wallet Hack, Says Galaxy Digital's Thorn
item.content:encoded: Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The crypto community is reeling from a breach involving "cold" Bitcoin wallets made by Coinkite. Hackers were able to steal an estimated $130 million worth of Bitcoin from about 7,300 wallet addresses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Surprising Truth About Instagram’s VHS Dates Videos
item.author: Sopan Deb and Maggie Shannon
item.content:encoded: The Instagram account advertises itself as resurfacing lost dating service videotapes from the 1980s. Social media users have been genuinely touched.

item.title: Sequoia Bets on Neros for American Drone Future (Correct)
item.content:encoded: Drone startup Neros has raised $250 million in a round co-led by Sequoia that triples its valuation to $2.5 billion as it expands beyond strike drones into autonomous systems and drone interceptors. CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson and Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire join Bloomberg to discuss plans to ramp up drone production, the race to build a US supply chain independent of China, and why they ultimately see a path to producing one million drones a year. They join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Corrects description of Sequoia’s involvement in Neros funding in headline.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The White House’s Secret A.I. Rules + The State of Model Alignment With METR’s Chris Painter + The Final Hot Mess Express
item.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Rowan Niemisto and Alyssa Moxley
item.content:encoded: A few details from the White House’s A.I. plan have leaked to the news media, but the administration has officially communicated almost nothing.

item.title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
item.author: Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: A co-founder of xAI is going all in on building open-source artificial intelligence so that “anyone can control and shape A.I. for their own needs.”

item.title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
item.author: Steven Lee Myers, Aida Alami and Carlos Barragán
item.content:encoded: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

item.title: Flock Cameras Are Dividing U.S. Cities. Here’s What to Know About Them.
item.author: Neil Vigdor
item.content:encoded: Flock Safety’s automated license plate-reading cameras, used by thousands of law enforcement agencies in the U.S., have drawn intense criticism from civil liberties groups.

item.title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
item.author: Rob Copeland and Kalley Huang
item.content:encoded: Six giant investment firms announced a $500 billion effort to raise money for customers of Nvidia to pay for computing power.

item.title: Google Team Tells Applicants Its HR Filters Are Unreliable
item.author: Julia Love
item.content:encoded: Alphabet Inc.’s Google pitches its artificial intelligence tools to corporate clients as a way to more quickly sift through a mountain of job applications to find the most promising candidates. Some of its own AI researchers don’t want to rely on these tools when recruiting.

item.title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
item.author: Emmy Martin
item.content:encoded: As Waymo deploys more driverless cars to 15 U.S. cities and counting, its vehicles keep encountering new and unexpected situations that they have no script to handle.

item.title: Meta Unveils an Open Version of Its Most Powerful A.I. Model
item.author: Eli Tan and Mike Isaac
item.content:encoded: The release of Muse Glimmer, a model that can be freely downloaded and modified, is likely to intensify a debate over whether A.I. should be restricted.

item.title: New Amazon Data Center Stokes Worry It Would Be the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.
item.author: Hiroko Tabuchi
item.content:encoded: The tech giant is investing in the natural-gas-burning power plant as part of a huge data center in Texas, even as it pledges to honor climate commitments.

item.title: Can A.I. Get You Where You Want to Go for Less?
item.author: Elaine Glusac
item.content:encoded: A wave of new services uses A.I. to monitor flights and hotel reservations to help you find lower prices. We look at how these tools work.

item.title: A.I.-Driven Chip Crunch Leads to New Rush of Lobbying in Washington
item.author: Kalley Huang and Ana Swanson
item.content:encoded: As data centers gobble up memory chips, other industries that need the components, including electronics companies like Apple and medical device makers, are asking for government help.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million Fine by New Mexico Judge
item.author: Eli Tan
item.content:encoded: The penalty, imposed by a state judge, is on top of a $375 million fine ordered by a jury that found Meta misled users about the safety of its platforms.

item.title: French Streamers Convicted in Case Related to Kick Livestream Death
item.author: Jonathan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The two men, users of the platform Kick, received suspended sentences and fines.

item.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
item.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.content:encoded: Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.

item.title: F.C.C. Removes Limit on Broadcast TV Ownership
item.author: Cecilia Kang
item.content:encoded: The move lifts a rule that said a single television-station owner could not reach more than 39 percent of U.S. households.

item.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation
item.author: Emmett Lindner
item.content:encoded: TikTok did not give a detailed reason for the layoffs, which will shutter its Nashville office.

item.title: How China’s A.I. Is Surging Across Africa
item.author: Paul Mozur, Adam Satariano and Aaron Krolik
item.content:encoded: In African tech hubs, developers are picking China’s cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over more powerful U.S. ones.

item.title: Google Names Demis Hassabis to New AI Role in a Leadership Shake-up
item.author: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: Minutes after four top researchers said they were leaving, Google said that Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning scientist who led the company’s A.I. lab, was stepping into a new job.

item.title: Four Top Google A.I. Researchers Form New Start-Up
item.author: Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: Jeff Dean, who for years was one of Google’s most important executives, is leading the new artificial intelligence company with the backing of Google.
